interpretation: Published angular astrometry transferred between two editions of the same 1997 HST photograph. The application distance is an explicitly adopted literature value; neither this transfer nor the accepted symmetry reconstruction measures depth or gas density.

publisherImage.credit: Bruce Balick (University of Washington), Vincent Icke (Leiden University, The Netherlands), Garrelt Mellema (Stockholm University), and NASA/ESA
publisherImage.licenseEvidence: Embedded xmpRights:UsageTerms in the pinned TIFF

wcs.orientationDescription: North is 113.6 degrees left of vertical in the displayed image. Preserve AVM/FITS pixel and rotation conventions when converting downward raster coordinates.

acceptedImage.cropDescription: The existing accepted lab recipe removes the white border and caption. It does not use the full 800x525 captioned image as the angular field.

imageTransfer.classification: derived approximate registration between published editions
imageTransfer.formula: For zero-based top-left pixel centers: nativeX=(acceptedX-6+0.5)*2769/788-0.5; nativeY=(acceptedY-6+0.5)*1540/438-0.5. Convert those native raster positions to the WCS pixel convention before projecting.

verification.comparison: Full pinned TIFF resampled to 788x438 versus the accepted APOD crop; no additional rotation, translation or crop fitted.
verification.limitations: Different resampling and JPEG noise remain. This is not an independent astrometric plate solution or a measurement of the publisher WCS uncertainty.

distance.reason: The 2024 ALMA study explicitly adopts 650 pc for consistency with earlier core studies and discusses the distance uncertainty. This choice is a documented model convention, not a new or definitive distance measurement.

alternatives.limitation: Depends on the interpretation of dusty-blob proper motions and kinematics. Its quoted 0.8 pc total nebular size must not be substituted for this photograph's smaller inner-lobe field.

references.title: Uncovering the structure and kinematics of the ionized core of M 2-9 with ALMA
references.evidenceLocation: Section 2, distance paragraph; Table 3 adopted distance
references.scope: The modeled ionized core is approximately 130 au across, much smaller than the full HST lobes. Its detailed geometry is not transferred to this reconstruction.

references.title: The evolution of M 2-9 from 2000 to 2010

excludedMetadata.reason: The page identifies M2-9 but displays incompatible object coordinates (10h19m32.2s, -60d13m30s). Use the pinned ESA image's own AVM instead.

limitations: This is the angular field of the accepted inner-lobe photograph, not the full faint nebula or remote polar blobs.
The existing zero-inclination symmetry prior and inferred depth remain authored reconstruction assumptions.
Angular astrometry does not establish a 3D stellar-membership catalogue; no synthetic star positions are added.
